human_tolerance.notes: Occurs in humid forest, forest edges, clearings and shady plantations; the sources do not describe use of urban areas.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Ecuador breeding recorded in February and March; other countries have different months.

vocalizations.description: A variable, almost random-sounding series of semimusical phrases given in a leisurely manner; the song differs regionally.
A clear ding-ding-ding, a chee!, an upslurred kuee and a more gravelly cheeur-cheeur. The source does not describe an alarm call; the program uses this call for alarms.

conservation.note: Wikipedia states IUCN Red List status Least Concern (IUCN 3.1).

range.note: Wikipedia: 'found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela'.

traits.limb_count.note: Birds have two legs; wings are counted separately by the schema convention.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Judgement: passerine; forages and moves among branches (Wikipedia: forages mid-level to canopy). Hop and fly are the modes the program uses.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Passerine bird; endothermy is a class-level fact not stated in the article.

traits.flight.note: Powered flight; Wikipedia's flight-based movement description implies it, but no explicit flight statement was captured.

traits.nest_type.note: Wikipedia describes a domed enclosure with a side entrance. The schema enum has no dome value; 'Cup' is the closest available and is a known limitation.

traits.perching.note: Passerine bird that forages in the canopy and at edges; perching is derived from that.

traits.size_class.note: Derived from mass_kg by the schema rule (Tiny below 0.05 kg).

traits.mass_kg.note: Scholer row X=801 mass column = 14.01, interpreted as grams for a single Peru population. Consistent with Wikipedia's 9 to 16 g range.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Wikipedia 'weighs 9 to 16 g' converted from grams to kilograms.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 9 to 11 cm length range, converted to metres.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Proxy: 1 / -ln(0.425) = 1.17 years, from one apparent annual adult survival estimate (0.425, se 0.123, Manu Biosphere Reserve, Peru, mark-recapture). Assumes constant annual survival (exponential lifetime). Apparent survival can be biased low by emigration, so the proxy is a rough lower-bound-type estimate. It is not a maximum or captive age, and the sources do not give a typical lifespan directly.

traits.diet.note: Authored allocation: Wikipedia says 'primarily small fruits' with 'smaller amounts of arthropods'. The 0.8/0.2 split is not quantified in the source.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia: 'mostly forages in pairs and regularly joins mixed-species feeding flocks'. The group size range is judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Judgement: daytime foraging; the sources do not state activity hours explicitly.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: small passerine; flees as in the shared program.

habitat.use.note: Wikipedia: occurs in the canopy and at edges, forages primarily mid-level to canopy and often down to the shrub layer in clearings and edges. The split is authored.

habitat.resources.note: Fruit and invertebrates follow the diet. Nest and shelter tags are authored from the nest description and canopy roosting; nest_cup is the closest available tag for a domed nest.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia describes forest, edges, clearings and shady plantations. Avoider is an authored reading; the article does not describe urban use.

seasonal.phases.note: Ecuador breeding in February and March per Wikipedia. The source is secondary, and the authored phase is limited to region EC.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Adult only. The clutch size, incubation and fledging periods are not known from the source.

vocalizations.song.note: Wikipedia's Ecuador description of the song.

vocalizations.call.note: Wikipedia's Ecuador description of the calls. The alarm role is authored because the source does not describe an alarm call.

activity.note: Fetched from GBIF and iNaturalist by tools/fetch_activity.py. See the activity.regions[].query entries.

behavior.note: Species-local program adapted from bt-perching-songbird-v1. The nest months are changed to February and March, and the food tag is changed to fruit. Authored.

look.note: Judgement, male plumage: blue-black upperparts, yellow underparts and forehead, grey tail. Wikipedia describes the plumage; the palette and proportions are authored.
